STUDYQURAN:24:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:intro/r6.claim: Verses 11–26 address the accusation of adultery against ʿĀʾishah, the Prophet's youngest wife, and the community's response to a slander declared baseless.
STUDYQURAN:24:intro/r6.anchor: against ʿĀʾishah, the youngest wife of the Prophet, and the response of the Muslim community to what was eventually declared to be a baseless slander

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r1.claim: Verses 11–26 expose hypocrites' role in the ifk scandal and give corrective warnings; negligent Muslims are cautioned, and accusations must not be believed without solid proof.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r1.anchor: Muslims who showed carelessness and negligence in this matter and thereby inadvertently strengthened the propaganda worked by the hypocrites are also warned

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p306/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p306/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p306/r3.claim: The section recalls the hypocrites’ ifk campaign and exposes how a group of Muslims unwittingly joined it and rashly spread their propaganda.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p306/r3.anchor: They inadvertently had become a part of this mischief and rather rashly started to spread the propaganda these hypocrites wanted to spread.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p306/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p306/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p306/r5.claim: The passage exposes hypocrites and their patrons trying to damage Muslims’ moral standing through rumors, and warns believers to guard against their efforts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p306/r5.anchor: the desire and effort of the hypocrites and their patronisers are exposed. Muslims must stand on guard against them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p313/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p313/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p313/r6.claim: The general warning reiterates the preceding directive against following Satan's path.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p313/r6.anchor: This verse sounds a similar warning to the Muslims like the ones that have already been sounded before.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r1.claim: Passing on unverified information follows conjecture, which is to follow Satan; people must not transmit claims whose truth they cannot establish.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r1.anchor: What is without proof is mere conjecture and to follow conjecture is to follow Satan.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r2.claim: Accepting baseless accusations reveals self-righteous vanity: purification comes only by God's grace, so no one should accuse others without investigation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r2.anchor: whoever attains purification does so merely because of God’s grace. If His graciousness is not present, none can be purified.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r3.claim: God hears and knows even people's hidden affairs, a reminder to those who give themselves excessive allowance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p314/r3.anchor: He hears and knows the most hidden things of people.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة وعيسى الهمداني وعيسى الثقفي وعاصم والأعمش
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r4.claim: These readers, and a report from ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash, use imāla in ما زكا.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r4.anchor: قراءة أبي جعفر وشيبة وعيسى الهمداني وعيسى الثقفي، ورويت عن عاصم والأعمش أيضا

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r5.claim: The form is from the wāw, as in زكوت تزكو, which accounts for imāla of its alif.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r5.anchor: من الواو، لقولهم فيه: زكوت تزكو فأميلت ألفه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r6.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r6.claim: Imāla is a kind of inflection, and verbs tolerate such change more than nouns because they have more forms; hence the examples العفا and السنا are less suitable for imāla.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r6.anchor: والأفعال أقعد في الاعتلال من الأسماء من حيث كانت كثيرة التصرف

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r7.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r7.speaker: علي والأعرج وعمرو بن عبيد وسلام وأبو السمال
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r7.claim: ʿAlī, al-Aʿraj, ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd, and Sallām read خطؤات with hamza; Abū al-Sammāl reads خطوات. Ibn Jinnī refers to an earlier discussion.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p105/r7.anchor: قراءة علي والأعرج وعمرو بن عبيد وسلام: "خطؤات"

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r1.claim: The expression 'steps of Satan' was previously explained, including its readings, in the commentary on al-Baqara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r1.anchor: تقدم الكلام على خطوات الشيطان تفسيرا وقراءة في البقرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r2.claim: The pronoun in 'he commands' returns to the conditional 'whoever'; fahsha is extreme ugliness, and munkar is what sound minds reject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r2.anchor: والضمير في فإنه عائد على من الشرطية، أي فإن متبع خطوات الشيطان يأمر بالفحشاء وهو ما أفرط قبحه والمنكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r3.claim: Without God's favor and mercy through purifying repentance, none would be purified.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r3.anchor: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته بالتوبة الممحصة ما طهر أحد منكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r4.claim: The majority read ma zaka with a light kaf; several other readers double the kaf and some apply imala.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ما زكى بتخفيف الكاف، وأمال حمزة والكسائي وأبو حيوة والحسن والأعمش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r5.claim: God purifies whom He wills, either those destined for felicity, whose good works signal it, or those whose sincere repentance He accepts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r5.anchor: ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء ممن سبقت له السعادة، وكان عمله الصالح أمارة على سبقها

JISHUMI:v7p5153/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r3.claim: Actions of the heart are accountable because love is a heart action to which a threat is attached.
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن أفعال القلب يؤخذ بها؛ لأن المحبة من أفعال القلب، وقد ألحق الوعيد به،

JISHUMI:v7p5153/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r4.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r4.claim: Abu ʿAlī holds that resolving to commit grave sin is itself grave sin and is like the intended act.
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r4.anchor: ولهذا قال شيخنا أبو علي: العزم على الفسق فسق، وهو مثل المعزوم عليه،

JISHUMI:v7p5153/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r5.speaker: أبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r5.claim: Abū Hāshim holds that resolve is less than the intended sin, though it can reach the level of grave sin.
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r5.anchor: وقال أبو هاشم: هو دونه، وقد يبلغ حد الفسق،

JISHUMI:v7p5153/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r6.claim: There is agreement that intending, desiring, approving, or loving disbelief is itself disbelief, since all are acts of the heart.
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r6.anchor: وأما العزم على الكفر فلا خلاف أنه كفر، وكذلك إرادة الكفر والرضى بالكفر، ومحبة الكفر، وكل ذلك من أفعال القلوب.

JISHUMI:v7p5153/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r7.speaker: ابن محيصن ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r7.claim: They read zakā with a doubled kāf, meaning to purify.
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r7.anchor: قرأ ابن محيصن ويعقوب: زكى بتشديد الكاف أي: طهر

JISHUMI:v7p5153/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r8.claim: The common reading has a light kāf and means purification from this sin.
JISHUMI:v7p5153/r8.anchor: وقراءة العامة بتخفيف الكاف، أي طهر: من هذا الذنب.

TABRISI:24:22-25/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:22-25/r1.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:24:22-25/r1.claim: One explanation says that no one among the addressees was purified from Satan’s whispering and made righteous by their own power.
TABRISI:24:22-25/r1.anchor: وقيل: معناه ما طهر منكم أحد من وسوسة الشيطان وما صلح

TABRISI:24:22-25/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:22-25/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:22-25/r2.claim: God purifies whomever He wills through His grace, acting with a favor that makes that person righteous before Him.
TABRISI:24:22-25/r2.anchor: أي يطهر بلطفه من يشاء وهو من له لطف يفعله سبحانه به ليزكو عنده

TABRISI:24:22-25/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:22-25/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:22-25/r3.claim: God hears people’s voices and words and knows their conditions and actions, and therefore acts for the good of morally responsible people.
TABRISI:24:22-25/r3.anchor: يفعل المصالح والألطاف بالمكلفين لأنه يسمع أصواتهم وأقوالهم ويعلم أحوالهم وأفعالهم

TABRISI:24:22-25/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:22-25/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:22-25/r4.claim: The verse shows that God wills the opposite of what Satan wills: since God condemns commands to indecency and evil, their creator and willing author would deserve even greater blame, which God is far above.
TABRISI:24:22-25/r4.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن الله سبحانه يريد من خلقه خلاف ما يريده الشيطان لأنه إذا ذم سبحانه الأمر بالفحشاء والمنكر فخالق الفحشاء والمنكر ومريدهما أولى بالذم تعالى وتقدس عن ذلك

TABRISI:24:22-25/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:22-25/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:22-25/r5.claim: No one becomes righteous except through God’s grace.
TABRISI:24:22-25/r5.anchor: وفيها دلالة على أن أحدا لا يصلح إلا بلطفه

SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r1.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ begins with parsing the pronoun as the pronoun of the matter.
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنها ضمير الشأن. وبه بدأ أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r2.claim: A second parse makes the pronoun refer to Satan.
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنها ضمير الشيطان. وهذان الوجهان

SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r3.claim: A third parse makes the pronoun return to the conditional relative man, whoever follows Satan.
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r3.anchor: والثالث: أنه عائد على " من " الشرطية

SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r4.claim: The matter-pronoun and Satan-reference parses are valid only for grammarians who do not require the conditional noun to have a resumptive pronoun in the answer clause.
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r4.anchor: وهذان الوجهان إنما يجوزان على رأي من لا يشترط

SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r5.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r5.claim: The majority read the kāf lightly, from zakā yazkū; its final alif is read with or without imāla.
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r5.anchor: العامة على تخفيف الكاف يقال: زكا يزكو

SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r6.speaker: الأعمش وأبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r6.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Abū Jaʿfar read the kāf doubled. The alif is written as yāʾ unusually, either reflecting imāla or spelling the doubled reading.
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r6.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وأبو جعفر بتشديدها. وكتبت ألفه

SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r7.claim: With the light reading, min aḥadin is the subject; with the doubled reading it is the object. Min is extra in either parse, and God is the subject in both.
SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r7.anchor: فعلى قراءة التخفيف يكون " من أحد " فاعلا

ASAD-NOTES:24:19#n23/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:24:19#n23/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:24:19#n23/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to verse 10 of this surah and its corresponding note 11.
ASAD-NOTES:24:19#n23/r1.anchor: See verse 10 of this surah and the corresponding note 11.

ASAD-NOTES:24:20#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:24:20#n24/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:24:20#n24/r1.claim: Here al-munkar has the same meaning as in 16:90, as explained in the corresponding note.
ASAD-NOTES:24:20#n24/r1.anchor: the term al-munkar has apparently the same meaning as in 16:90

ASAD-NOTES:24:20#n24/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:24:20#n24/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:24:20#n24/r2.claim: The warning addresses people who accuse others of moral failings while forgetting that only God's grace lets inherently weak humans remain pure.
ASAD-NOTES:24:20#n24/r2.anchor: imputing moral failings to others and forgetting that it is only due to God's grace that man, in his inborn weakness, can ever remain pure.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r3.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisāʾī agree to leave these cited forms without imāla.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r3.anchor: واتفقنا يعني حمزة والكسائي على ترك الإمالة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ثم دنا ﴾ النجم 8

QIRAAT-ER:24:21:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:24:21:7#1/r1.speaker: skn
QIRAAT-ER:24:21:7#1/r1.claim: Sukūn on ṭāʾ removes the intervening vowel, making a heavier consonant cluster that may stress the physical thud of a step.
QIRAAT-ER:24:21:7#1/r1.anchor: skn, mutawatir: Sukūn on ṭāʾ — reduces the vowel between ṭ and w, creating a heavier consonant cluster

QIRAAT-ER:24:21:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:24:21:12#1/r1.speaker: skn
QIRAAT-ER:24:21:12#1/r1.claim: The same sukūn variant occurs at the second occurrence, maintaining the reading across both words.
QIRAAT-ER:24:21:12#1/r1.anchor: skn, mutawatir: Same sukūn variant as word 7 — consistent across both occurrences

ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r1.claim: Following Satan's footsteps is a metonym for following him and obeying his whispers in every action and omission, including spreading and desiring indecency.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r1.anchor: أي لا تسلكوا مسالكه في كل ما تأتون وما تذرون والكلام كناية عن اتباع الشيطان

ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r2.speaker: نافع والبزي برواية ابن ربيعة وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر وحمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r2.claim: These readers pronounce the ṭāʾ of خطوات with sukūn; another reading has fatḥa.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r2.anchor: في رواية ابن ربيعة عنه وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر وحمزة ( خطوات ) بسكون الطاء

ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r3.claim: In both readings, خطوات is the plural of خطوة, the distance between the feet; خطوة with fatḥa on khāʾ is instead the verbal noun of stepping. The plural normally moves the medial vowel to distinguish a noun from an adjective.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r3.anchor: وهو في جميع ذلك جمع خطوة بضم الخاء وسكون الطاء اسم لما بين القدمين

ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r4.claim: Repeating the explicit nouns instead of saying ومن يتبعها or من يتبعه intensifies and reinforces the warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r4.anchor: وضع الظاهر أن موضع ضميري الخطوات والشيطان حيث لم يقل ومن يتبعها أو من يتبع خطواته

ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r5.claim: الفحشاء is what is extremely vile; المنكر is what religious law condemns.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r5.anchor: ما ينكره الشرع وضمير إنه للشيطان وقيل للشأن

ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r6.claim: The pronoun in فإنه can refer to Satan or to the matter; one analysis posits an omitted conditional answer supplied by what follows, originally explaining the prohibition. Grammarians object that answers are omitted only after past conditions, citing a line beginning لئن تك قد ضاقت علي بيوتكم; the response is that here the following clause itself stands in the answer's place.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r6.anchor: وضمير إنه للشيطان وقيل للشأن وجواب الشرط مقدر سد ما بعد الفاء مسده

ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan says the pronoun refers to the conditional clause, with no ellipsis: whoever follows Satan becomes a leader in misguidance who commands indecency; this assumes a nominative conditional answer must contain a returning pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r7.anchor: الضمير عائد على الشرطية ولم يعتبر في الكلام حذفا أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r8.claim: God's favor includes the clear revealed signs, guidance to repentance that cleanses sins, and the institution of legal penalties that expiate sins other than apostasy according to a group of scholars.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r8.anchor: بما من جملته إنزال هاتيك الآيات البينات والتوفيق للتوبة الممحصة من الذنوب

ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r9.speaker: جمع
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r9.claim: A group holds that legal penalties expiate sins other than apostasy; they answer the earlier Abu Hurayra report by saying it predates revelation of this ruling to the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r9.anchor: شرع الحدود المكفر لما عدا الردة منها على ما ذهب إليه جمع وأجابوا عن حديث أبي هريرة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r10.claim: زكى means becoming purified from the stain of sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r10.anchor: أي ما طهر من دنس الذنوب

ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r1.speaker: روح والأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r1.claim: Ruh and al-Aʿmash read زكى with gemination and imāla.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r1.anchor: وقرأ روح والأعمش ( ما زكى ) بالتشديد والإمالة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r2.claim: The ungeminated زكى is written with yāʾ despite its wāw root because it can undergo imāla or by analogy with the geminated form, as Abu Hayyan notes.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r2.anchor: المخفف بالياء مع أنه من ذوات الواو وحقها أن تكتب بالألف

ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r3.claim: منكم is explanatory; من أحد is extra for emphasis. أحد is nominative as subject in one reading, but accusative as object in the other, with God as its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r3.anchor: و ( أحد ) في حيز الرفع على الفاعلية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r4.claim: أبدا means ever, without an endpoint.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r5.claim: God purifies whom He chooses by granting grace and mercy, enabling repentance and accepting it, as He did with those involved in the slander who were free of hypocrisy.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r5.anchor: من عباده بإفاضة فضله ورحمته عليه وحمله على التوبة وقبولها منه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r6.claim: God hears all speech, including their expressed repentance, and knows all things, including their intentions.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r6.anchor: مبالغ في سمعه الأقوال التي من جملتها ما أظهروه من التوبة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r7.claim: The verse urges sincerity in repentance; repeating the explicit divine name evokes God's divinity as grounds of hearing and knowledge and strengthens the concluding clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r7.anchor: وفيه حث لهم على الإخلاص في التوبة وإظهار الاسم الجليل للإيذان باستدعاء الألوهية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r3.claim: Following Satan's steps leads him to command indecent acts and what God disapproves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r3.anchor: ومن يتبع خطوات الشيطان فإنه يأمر بالفحشاء والمنكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r4.claim: Fahsha means vile or repugnant actions.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r5.anchor: والمنكر} ما يكرهه الله عز وجل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r6.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r6.claim: Muqatil glosses zakā as becoming sound or righteous.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses zakā as becoming pure.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r8.claim: Some exegetes read this generally: without God's favor and protective grace, no one among them would be sound or upright.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r8.anchor: والآية على العموم عند بعض المفسرين، قالوا: أخبر الله أنه لولا فضله ورحمته بالعصمة ما صلح منكم أحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r9.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r9.claim: Another group takes the address to concern those involved in the slander: after their deed, none would be purified of that sin or have their affairs set right.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: هذا الخطاب للذين خاضوا في الإفك، ومعناه: ما طهر من هذا الذنب ولا صلح أمره بعد الذي فعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r10.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r10.claim: In a transmission through Ata, Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as meaning that no one's repentance would have been accepted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r10.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء، قال: ما قبل توبة أحد منكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r11.claim: God purifies from sin whomever He wills through mercy and forgiveness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p26/r11.anchor: ولكن الله يزكي} يطهر، {من يشاء} من الذنب بالرحمة والمغفرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:18-21/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:18-21/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:18-21/r6.claim: Repeating the mention of God's favor and mercy recalls His delay of punishment, underscoring the offense's gravity.

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:18-21/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:18-21/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:18-21/r7.claim: The clause that God is compassionate and merciful is coordinated with His favor; the conditional answer is omitted because already stated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:18-21/r7.anchor: على حصول فضله ورحمته عليهم وحذف الجواب وهو مستغنى عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r1.claim: Here following Satan's steps means spreading indecency.

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r2.claim: The word is also read with an open ṭāʾ; Nāfiʿ, al-Bazzī, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Bakr, and Ḥamza read it with sukūn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r2.anchor: وقرىء بفتح الطاء وقرأ نافع والبزي وأبو عمرو

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r3.claim: The following clause explains why following Satan is prohibited.

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r5.claim: Munkar is what religious law rejects.

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r6.claim: God's favor includes enabling repentance that erases sins and prescribing penalties that expiate them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r6.anchor: بتوفيق التوبة الماحية للذنوب وشرع الحدود

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r7.claim: Zakā means purification from the stain of sin, forever.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r7.anchor: ما طهر من دنسها. { منكم من أحد أبدا } آخر الدهر

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r8.claim: God purifies whom He wills by guiding that person to repentance and accepting it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r9.claim: God hears what they say and knows their intentions.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r7.claim: The believers are urged to make every effort not to imitate Satan or follow any path he beautifies; the verb form also hints at pardon for inadvertent slips.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r7.anchor: لا تقتدوا به ولا تسلكوا مسالكه التي يحمل على سلوكها بتزيينها في شيء من الأشياء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r8.claim: The repeated explicit phrase, instead of a pronoun, heightens aversion; following Satan is framed as deliberate resolve rather than mistake or forgetfulness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r8.anchor: بعزم ثابت من غير أن يكون مخطئا أو ناسيا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r9.claim: Satan commands extreme ugliness and whatever the law does not permit; he aims first at the greatest deviation and descends to lesser evil if thwarted.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r9.anchor: فإن لم يصل تنزل إلى أدناه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r10.claim: One who follows Satan takes on his deeds and sinks to utter baseness; spelling out Satan again makes the warning stronger than a pronoun would.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r10.anchor: عمل بعمله , فصار في غاية السفول

BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r1.claim: God's favor purifies souls and lifts them above base desires, while His mercy grants repentance that expiates the deficient speech and low actions ignorance caused.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r1.anchor: بإكرامكم ورفعتكم بشرع التوبة المكفرة لما جر إليه الجهل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r2.claim: Zakkā means to purify and cause to grow; the repeated min emphasizes that not one person is excluded, and abadan extends the denial across all time.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r3.claim: God alone purifies whom He wills from the soul's impurities and heart's diseases: He protected some from the slander and left others to fail.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r4.claim: God hears every utterance and knows thoughts, states, and deeds, so He knows who is fit for purification; believers should thank Him and patiently continue kindness toward others.

DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r7.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r7.claim: The footsteps of Satan mean Satan's embellishment and enticement.

DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r8.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r8.claim: Fahisha means sins; munkar means what is not recognized as right, such as the accusation made against Aisha.
DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r8.anchor: {فإنه يأمر بالفحشاء} يعني بالمعاصي {والمنكر} ما لا يعرف مثل ما قيل لعائشة

DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r9.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r9.claim: Zaka means becoming righteous: without God's favor and mercy, none of them would ever have become righteous.

DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r10.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r10.claim: God makes righteous whomever He wills.

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas is quoted saying that Ali is the foremost, chief, and leader of every Qur'anic address to believers, and that the Companions were censured in the Qur'an except Ali.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : ما في القران آية يا ايها الذين امنوا الا ان عليا شريفها وسيدها واميرها

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r2.speaker: أبو رافع
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r2.claim: After a wife swore that she would be Jewish, Christian, and free her slaves unless he divorced his wife, Ibn Umar, Zaynab bint Abi Salama, and Asim ibn Umar called the vow Satan's steps.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال : غضبت علي امراتي فقالت : هي يوم يهودية ، ويوم نصرانية ، وكل مملوك لها حر ان لم تطلق امراتك

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud told a man who had vowed never to eat udder that this was Satan's step; he should eat and expiate his oath.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r3.anchor: عن مسروق قال : اتي عبد الله بضرع وملح فجعل ياكل ، فاعتزل رجل من القوم ، فقال ابن مسعود : ناولوا صاحبكم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains Satan's steps as his deeds or actions.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : خطوات الشيطان يقول : عمله

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r5.speaker: مسروق
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r5.claim: For a man who vowed to sacrifice his son, Masruq ruled that it was Satan's step and directed him to sacrifice a ram instead.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r5.anchor: عن الشعبي ، في رجل نذر ان يذبح ابنه ، قال : افتاه مسروق قال : هي من خطوات الشيطان ، وافتاه بكبش

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r6.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r6.claim: Ikrima explains Satan's steps as his promptings or impulses.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2551#2/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة خطوات الشيطان قال : نزعات الشيطان

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r1.claim: Qatada says every act of disobedience is one of Satan's steps.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r1.anchor: سالت قتادة ، عن قول الله عز وجل قلت : ارايت قول الله : لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان .

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r2.speaker: أبو مجلز
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r2.claim: Abu Majliz identifies Satan's steps as vows made to commit sins or involving sinful acts.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r2.anchor: عن أبي مجلز في قول الله : لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان قال : النذور في المعاصي أو بالمعاصي

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says this refers to Satan's embellishment of the false accusation against Aisha.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير : لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان يعني : تزيين الشيطان في قذف عائشة رضي الله عنها

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r4.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r4.claim: Abu Malik similarly applies the steps to Satan's embellishment of the accusation against Aisha; fahsha means sins, and munkar means what is rejected, such as that accusation.

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses fahsha as fornication and munkar as shirk; al-Hasan and Ikrima are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : الفحشاء يقول : الزنا والمنكر . يقول : الشرك ، وروى عن الحسن وعكرمة مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains God's favor here as a bestowal from God.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r6.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق : قوله ولولا فضل الله اي من الله

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r7.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains God's favor and mercy as His blessing.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله : ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته يعني ونعمته

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r8.claim: No human can guide himself through beneficial good or protect himself from harm through his own power; purification and guidance depend on God's favor.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2552/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ما زكى منكم من أحد ابدا يقول : ما اهتدى أحد من الخلائق بشيء من الخير ينفع به نفسه ، ولم يتق شيئا من الشر

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses «was purified» as «none of you ever became sound or righteous».
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : ما زكى يعني ما صلح منكم من أحد ابدا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says «was purified» means «became Muslim» and that every Qurʾanic use of zakā or tazakkā means Islam.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r2.anchor: سمعت ابن زيد في قول الله : ما زكى منكم من أحد ابدا قال : ما اسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains that God sets right whomever He wills.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء يعني يصلح من يشاء

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r4.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r4.claim: The commentary says the explanation of «God is Hearing, Knowing» was given earlier, at 24:22.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2553/r4.anchor: قوله : والله سميع عليم قد تقدم تفسيره قوله تعالى : ولا ياتل اولوا الفضل منكم آية 22

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p186/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p186/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p186/r1.claim: Coming after the ten verses about the slander, this warning identifies their prohibitions, evil suspicions, and wish to spread indecency as satanic whisperings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p186/r1.anchor: وقوعه عقب الآيات العشر التي في قضية الإفك مشير إلى أن ما تضمنته تلك الآيات من المناهي وظنون السوء ومحبة شيوع الفاحشة كله من وساوس الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p186/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p186/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p186/r2.claim: The command depicts satanic whispering as Satan walking and a person obeying as following his steps, making an unseen mental influence into a perceptible scene.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p186/r2.anchor: فشبه حال فاعلها في كونه متلبسا بوسوسة الشيطان بهيئة الشيطان يمشي والعامل بأمره يتبع خطى ذلك الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, and al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr read ṭāʾ with sukūn; the other readers vocalize it with ḍamma, also a common permissible form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r1.anchor: قرأه نافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم والبزي عن ابن كثير بسكون الطاء كما هي في المفرد فهو جمع سلامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r2.claim: A khuṭwah is one step: moving the foot that trailed behind forward past the other foot.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r2.anchor: والخطوة بضم الخاء : اسم لنقل الماشي إحدى قدميه التي كانت متأخرة عن القدم الأخرى وجعلها متقدمة عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r3.claim: Man is conditional here, so all readers agree that yatbaʿ is jussive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r3.anchor: و ( من ) شرطية ولذلك وقع فعل { يتبع } مجزوما باتفاق القراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r4.claim: The clause beginning fa-innahu is the conditional response; its link is the omitted general object of “commands,” which includes the one who follows Satan, and both pronouns refer to Satan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r4.anchor: وجملة : { فإنه يأمر بالفحشاء والمنكر } جواب الشرط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r5.claim: Anyone following Satan's way falls into indecency and wrong, since Satan commands people to commit both and the follower is included in that general address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r5.anchor: والمعنى : ومن يتبع خطوات الشيطان يفعل الفحشاء والمنكر لأن الشيطان يأمر الناس بالفحشاء والمنكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r6.claim: Al-faḥshāʾ is any ugly deed or utterance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r6.anchor: والفحشاء : كل فعل أو قول قبيح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r7.claim: Al-munkar is what the revealed law and people of virtue reject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r7.anchor: والمنكر : ما تنكره الشريعة وينكره أهل الخير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r1.claim: Without God's guidance to good and forgiveness upon repentance, no person would attain purity: Satan's trial is formidable and few could escape it unaided by religious guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r1.anchor: أي لولا فضله بأن هداكم إلى الخير ورحمته بالمغفرة عند التوبة ما كان أحد من الناس زاكيا لأن فتنة الشيطان فتنة عظيمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r2.claim: The familiar reading has a light kāf; the word ends in wāw and has no imālah, so its expected spelling is a plain alif although the muṣḥaf draws the alif in yāʾ form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r2.anchor: و { زكى } بتخفيف الكاف على المشهور من القراءات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r3.claim: This spelling does not conflict with the muṣḥaf: only a change to the pronounced letters would do so, while transmission safeguards performance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r3.anchor: ولا تعد قراءته بتخفيف الكاف مخالفة لرسم المصحف لأن المخالفة المضعفة للقراءة هي المخالفة المؤدية إلى اختلاف النطق بحروف الكلمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p188/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p188/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p188/r1.claim: The closing dictum joins promise and threat: God hears those spreading indecency and knows their wish to do so, and hears and knows those who condemn it, rewarding each for their deeds.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p188/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p188/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p188/r2.claim: Naming God explicitly makes the closing statement stand on its own like a proverb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p188/r2.anchor: وإظهار اسم الجلالة فيه ليكون التذييل مستقلا بنفسه لأنه مما يجري مجرى المثل

BURSEVI:v6p93/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93/r1.claim: God’s immense generosity and mercy purify people of blameworthy traits despite their deserving punishment; He created them for mercy, while punishment follows their bad choices.
BURSEVI:v6p93/r1.anchor: غاية كرم الله ورحمته وفضله على عباده حيث يتفضل عليهم ويرحمهم ويزكيهم عن أوصافهم الذميمة مع استحقاقهم العذاب الأليم

BURSEVI:v6p93/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93/r2.claim: With damma, khutwah is the distance between the feet; with fatha, one stride. Following footsteps idiomatically means adopting someone’s way, here Satan’s course.
BURSEVI:v6p93/r2.anchor: جمع خطوة بضم الخاء وهي ما بين القدمين أي ما بين رجلي الخاطي وبالفتح المرة الواحدة من الخطو

BURSEVI:v6p93/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93/r3.claim: Believers must not follow paths Satan whispers into their hearts and beautifies to their eyes, including spreading or cherishing scandal.
BURSEVI:v6p93/r3.anchor: والمعنى لا تسلكوا الطرق التي يدعوكم إليها الشيطان ويوسوس بها في قلوبكم ويزينها لأعينكم

BURSEVI:v6p93/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93/r4.claim: Fahshaʾ is what is extremely ugly by custom or reason, in word or deed; munkar is what the Law rejects, while Abu Layth says it is unknown to scripture and sunnah.
BURSEVI:v6p93/r4.anchor: والفحشاء والفاحشة ما عظم قبحه عرفا وعقلا سواء كان فعلا أو قولا والمنكر ما ينكره الشرع

BURSEVI:v6p93/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93/r5.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v6p93/r5.claim: Abu Layth defines munkar as what is not recognized in a revealed law or the Sunna.
BURSEVI:v6p93/r5.anchor: أبو الليث : المنكر ما لا يعرف في شريعة ولا سنة

BURSEVI:v6p93/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93/r6.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p93/r6.claim: Al-Mufradat includes what sound reason deems ugly or leaves undecided, provided the Law judges it ugly.
BURSEVI:v6p93/r6.anchor: المفردات" : المنكر كل شيء تحكم العقول الصحيحة بقبحه أو تتوقف في استقباحه العقول

BURSEVI:v6p93/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93/r7.claim: Calling Satan’s beautifying and goading an “order” belittles the followers who heed him.
BURSEVI:v6p93/r7.anchor: واستعير الأمر لتزيينه وبعثه لهم على الشر تحقيرا لشأنهم

BURSEVI:v6p93/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93/r8.claim: God’s favor includes these explanations, enabling repentance that erases sins, and the institution of legal penalties that expiate them; without this, no one would be purified.
BURSEVI:v6p93/r8.anchor: بهذه البيانات والتوفيق للتوبة الماحية للذنوب وشرع الحدود المكفرة لها

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r1.claim: In min kum min ahad, the first min is explanatory; the second is extra, and ahad is nominative as the subject.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r1.anchor: من الأولى بيانية والثانية زائدة واحد في حيز الرفع على الفاعلية

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r2.claim: Abadan means for all time, without end.

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r3.claim: God purifies whom He wills by bestowing the effects of grace and mercy, guiding the person to repentance and accepting it, as He did for them.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r3.anchor: من عباده بإفاضة آثار فضله ورحمته عليه وحمله على التوبة ثم قبولها منه كما فعل بكم

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r4.claim: The verse refutes the Qadariyya, who claim souls are purified through acts of worship without God’s enabling.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r4.anchor: وفيه حجة على القدرية فإنهم زعموا أن طهارة النفوس بالطاعات والعبادات من غير توفيق من الله

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r5.claim: God hears their words, including the slander and their expressed repentance, and knows their intentions; this urges sincere repentance.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r5.anchor: مبالغ في سمع الأقوال التي من جملتها ما قالوه من حديث الإفك وما أظهروه من التوبة منه

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r6.claim: Satan’s many steps encompass every indecency and wrong, including slander, insults, lies, and searching out people’s faults.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r6.anchor: أن خطوات الشيطان كثيرة وهي جملة ما يطلق عليه الفحشاء والمنكر ومن جملته القذف والشتم والكذب وتفتيش عيوب الناس

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r7.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r7.claim: A hadith says human speech is against its speaker except speech commanding right, forbidding wrong, or remembering God.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث : "كلام ابن آدم كله عليه لاله إلا أمرا بمعروف

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r8.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r8.claim: A hadith calls it great treachery to tell a brother something he trusts while lying to him.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث : "كثرت خيانة أن تحدث أخاك حديثا هو لك به مصدق وأنت له كاذب

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r9.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r9.claim: A hadith praises the person whose own faults keep him occupied instead of other people’s faults.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث : "طوبى لمن شغله عيبه عن عيوب الناس

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r10.claim: The practical counsel is to spend from lawful earnings, associate with jurists and wise people, and avoid the ignorant and sinful.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r10.anchor: وأنفق من مال اكتسبه من غير معصية وخالط أهل الفقه والحكمة وجانب أهل الجهل والمعصية

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r11.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r11.claim: Some interpret Satan’s steps as vows to disobey God; vows to obey, such as prayer or fasting, are excluded because they prevent indecency and wrong.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r11.anchor: وعن بعضهم خطوات الشيطان النذور في معصية الله

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r12.claim: Purification ultimately belongs to God, who enables obedience by grace, yet a student needs a teacher to learn purification according to God’s intent; the Prophet is the greatest means.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r12.anchor: أمر التزكية إنما هو إلى الله فإنه بفضله ورحمته وفق العبد للطاعات

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r13.speaker: عبد الله الأنصاري
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r13.claim: Abdullah al-Ansari says he had many hadith and law teachers, but Abu al-Hasan al-Kharaqani taught him the spiritual path; without meeting him, he would not have known reality.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r13.anchor: قال شيخ الإسلام عبد الله الأنصاري قدس سره : مشايخي في علم الحديث وعلم الشريعة

BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r14.speaker: عبد الله الأنصاري
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r14.claim: Spiritual guides lead along the religious path and unlock certainty; the perfected human’s presence and companionship are a great blessing.
BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r14.anchor: فأهل الإرشاد هداة طريق الدين ومفاتيح أبواب اليقين فوجود الإنسان الكامل غنيمة ومجالسته نعمة عظيمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r1.claim: “Khuṭuwāt” is the plural of “khuṭwa,” a step between the feet; the warning means not to walk Satan's paths of evil actions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r1.anchor: وخطوات جمع خطوة وهي ما بين القدمين في المشي فكأن المعنى لا تمشوا في سبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r2.speaker: منذر بن سعيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r2.claim: Mundhir ibn Saʿīd suggests “khuṭuwāt” may instead be a plural of “khaṭaʾ,” meaning a misdeed, with the hamza eased in pronunciation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r2.anchor: وقال منذر بن سعيد يجوز أن يكون خطوات جمع خطأ من الخبيثة، وسهلت الهمزة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r3.claim: The majority read “khuṭuwāt” with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r4.speaker: عاصم والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r4.claim: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read the ṭāʾ of “khuṭuwāt” with sukūn.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r5.claim: The majority read “mā zakā” with a light kāf, meaning no one would be guided, enter Islam, or know right guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «ما زكى» ، بتخفيف الكاف أي ما اهتدى ولا أسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r6.speaker: أبو حيوة والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r6.claim: Abū Ḥaywa and al-Ḥasan read with a doubled kāf: God's purification and guidance are by grace, not earned through deeds or avoiding sins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة والحسن «زكى» بشد الكاف أي تزكيته لكم وتطهيره وهدايته إنما هي بفضله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r7.claim: God purifies whom He wills among those destined for felicity; their righteous deeds are signs of that prior destiny.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r7.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى أنه يزكي من يشاء ممن سبقت له السعادة وكان عمله الصالح أمارة على سبق السعادة له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r8.claim: God hears all their speech, including slander, and knows what is true or false without error.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p172/r8.anchor: سميع لجميع أقوالهم وكلامهم من قذف وغيره، عليم بحق ذلك من باطله لا يجوز عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r2.claim: The devil's footsteps are his ways and paths, and what he commands.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r2.anchor: يعني: طرائقه ومسالكه وما يأمر به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r3.claim: The warning is expressed in language Ibn Kathir describes as exceptionally clear, concise, forceful, and beautiful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r3.anchor: هذا تنفير وتحذير من ذلك، بأفصح العبارة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the devil's footsteps as his deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r4.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {خطوات الشيطان} : عمله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r5.claim: Ikrima explains the devil's footsteps as his incitements or insinuations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r5.anchor: وقال عكرمة: نزغاته. وقال قتادة: كل معصية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r6.claim: Qatada says every sin belongs to the devil's footsteps.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: كل معصية فهي من خطوات الشيطان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r7.speaker: أبو مجلز
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r7.claim: Abu Mijlaz counts vows to commit sins among the devil's footsteps.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r7.anchor: وقال أبو مجلز: النذور في المعاصي من خطوات الشيطان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r8.claim: When a man vowed to abstain from food, Ibn Masud called this a satanic impulse and told him to expiate his oath and eat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r8.anchor: وقال مسروق: سأل رجل ابن مسعود فقال: إني حرمت أن آكل طعاما؟ فقال: هذا من نزعات الشيطان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r9.speaker: الشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r9.claim: When a man vowed to slaughter his son, al-Shabi called it a satanic whisper and instructed him to sacrifice a ram.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r9.anchor: وقال الشعبي في رجل نذر ذبح ولده: هذا من نزغات الشيطان،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r10.speaker: أبو رافع
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r10.claim: Abu Rafi reports that Ibn Umar, Zaynab bint Umm Salama, and Asim ibn Umar all judged his wife's conditional vows to become Jewish or Christian and free her slaves a satanic impulse, not grounds to divorce.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r10.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال: غضبت علي امرأتي فقالت: هي يوما يهودية، ويوما نصرانية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r11.claim: Without God's favor, no one would attain purity or good: God grants repentance and return, purifying souls from association, immorality, and bad traits to differing degrees.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r11.anchor: لولا هو يرزق من يشاء التوبة والرجوع إليه، ويزكي النفوس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r12.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r12.claim: God purifies whom He wills among creation and misguides and casts whom He wills into the hazards of error.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r12.anchor: أي: من خلقه، ويضل من يشاء ويرديه في مهالك الضلال والغي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30#2/r1.claim: God hears His servants' words and knows which of them deserves guidance or misguidance.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p225#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p225#4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p225#4/r1.claim: The verse repeats the reminder of God’s favor in not hastening punishment and omits the conditional answer as earlier; repeating the omission intensifies emphasis, as with al-Tawwāb, al-Raʾūf, and al-Raḥīm.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p225#4/r1.anchor: وكرر المنة بترك المعاجلة بالعقاب ، حاذفا جواب لولا كما حذفه ثمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r1.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Salam interprets Satan's steps as Satan's sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : خطايا الشيطان , قاله يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r2.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r2.claim: Ibn Shajara interprets them as Satan's traces or footprints.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r3.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿIsa describes them as Satan's progression from lawful acts to forbidden ones and from obedience to disobedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r3.anchor: الثالث : هو تخطي الشيطان الحلال إلى الحرام والطاعة إلى المعصية , قاله ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r4.speaker: أبو مجلز
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r4.claim: Abu Majliz interprets Satan's steps as vows to commit sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r4.anchor: الرابع : هو النذور في المعاصي , قاله أبو مجلز .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r5.claim: Al-Mawardi suggests the phrase can describe moving from one sin to another, like a foot stepping from place to place.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p82#2/r5.anchor: ويحتمل خامسا : أن تكون خطوات الشيطان الانتقال من معصية إلى أخرى مأخوذ من نقل القدم بالخطو من مكان إلى مكان .

MUQATIL:24:21-22/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r1.claim: Satan's steps here are his embellishment of the accusation against Aisha.
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r1.anchor: يعني تزيين الشيطان في قذف عائشة، رضي الله عنها، { ومن يتبع خطوات الشيطان

MUQATIL:24:21-22/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r2.claim: Al-fahshaʾ means sins, and al-munkar means what is not recognized.
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r2.anchor: ومن يتبع خطوات الشيطان فإنه يأمر بالفحشآء } يعني بالمعاصى { والمنكر } يعني ما لا يعرف

MUQATIL:24:21-22/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r3.claim: God's favor and mercy here mean His bounty.
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r3.anchor: { ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته } يعني نعمته { ما زكا

MUQATIL:24:21-22/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r4.claim: Zakā means to become sound or righteous; no one would be made righteous without God's grace and mercy.
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r4.anchor: { ما زكا } يعني ما صلح { منكم من أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي

MUQATIL:24:21-22/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r5.claim: God makes righteous whomever He wills.
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r5.anchor: ولكن الله يزكي } يعني يصلح { من يشآء والله سميع

MUQATIL:24:21-22/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r6.claim: God hears what they said about Aisha and knows it.
MUQATIL:24:21-22/r6.anchor: والله سميع } لقولهم لعائشة { عليم } [آية: 21] به.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r1.claim: Satan’s steps are his traces and whispers, followed by listening to the slander and talking about it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r1.anchor: أى آثاره ووساوسه بالاصغاء إلى الافك والقول فيه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r2.claim: Fahshāʾ is what is extremely vile.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r3.claim: Munkar is what people’s souls reject, recoil from, and disapprove.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r3.anchor: ما تنكره النفوس فتنفر عنه ولا ترتضيه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r4.claim: Without God’s favor and mercy in granting expiatory repentance, none would have been purified of the slander’s sin thereafter.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r4.anchor: تفضل عليكم بالتوبة الممحصة لما طهر منكم أحد آخر الدهر من أثم الافك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r5.claim: God purifies those who repent by accepting their sincere repentance.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r5.anchor: يطهر التائبين بقبول توبتهم إذا محضوها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r6.claim: God hears what people say and knows their inner selves and sincerity.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r6.anchor: ﴿ والله سميع ﴾ لقولهم ﴿ عليم ﴾ بضمائرهم وإخلاصهم

QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r1.claim: The steps of Satan are his paths and ways; believers must not follow the route he invites them to take.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r1.anchor: يعني مسالكه ومذاهبه المعنى: لا تسلكوا الطريق الذي يدعوكم إليها الشيطان

QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r2.claim: A khutwa is the distance between two feet; khutwa with fatḥa is the verbal noun of stepping, and its plural is khutuwāt. The text also explains takhaṭṭā as crossing over to someone and cites a Friday-row crossing report.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r2.anchor: وواحد الخطوات خطوة، وهو ما بين القدمين. والخطوة بالفتح المصدر يقال: خطوت خطوة، وجمعها خطوات

QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r3.speaker: الجمهور وعاصم والأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r3.claim: The majority read khutuwāt with the ṭāʾ vowelled u; ʿAsim and al-Aʿmash read it with the ṭāʾ quiescent.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «خطوات» بضم الطاء. وسكنها عاصم والأعمش

QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r4.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r4.claim: The majority read zakā with an ungeminated kāf, meaning that none would be guided, accept Islam, or recognize right guidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r4.anchor: بتخفيف الكاف أي ما اهتدى ولا أسلم ولا عرف رشدا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r5.claim: An alternative meaning of zakā is to become sound or righteous, from zakā yazkū zakāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r5.anchor: أي ما صلح يقال: زكا يزكو زكاء أي صلح

QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r6.speaker: الحسن وأبو حيوة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu Haywa read the verb with a geminated kāf: God alone purifies, guides, and cleanses people by His favor, not through their deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r6.anchor: وشددها الحسن وأبو حيوة أي أن تزكيته لكم وتطهيره وهدايته إنما هي بفضله لا بأعمالكم

QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r7.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r7.claim: Al-Kisaʾi treats the prohibition against following Satan as parenthetical; “none of you would ever be purified” answers both that clause and the preceding “were it not for God’s favor.”
QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r7.anchor: وقال الكسائي: { يأيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان }

RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r1.claim: The first clause has an omitted apodosis, possibly that they would have perished, been punished, or destroyed.
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r1.anchor: أن جوابه محذوف وكأنه قال لهلكتم أو لعذبكم الله

RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the address is to Ḥassān, Misṭaḥ, and Ḥamna, though it may be general.
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس الخطاب لحسان ومسطح وحمنة

RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r3.claim: One analysis makes the apodosis the following statement that no one would ever have been purified.
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r3.anchor: والثاني : جوابه في قوله : { زكى منكم من أحد أبدا }

RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r4.claim: Abū Muslim proposes that indecency would spread and its harm become great without God’s favor and mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r4.anchor: لكانت الفاحشة تشيع فتعظم المضرة وهو قول أبي مسلم

RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r5.claim: Rāzī prefers an omitted apodosis: intervening speech separates the later clause from the first. God preserved, delayed, and enabled repentance; in mercy He does not withhold what benefits a servant, even when that servant wrongs himself.
RAZI-FULL:v23p160#2/r5.anchor: والأقرب أن جوابه محذوف لأن قوله من بعد

RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r1.claim: Khuṭuwāt is read with ḍamma on ṭāʾ or with it quiescent.

RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r2.claim: Khuṭuwāt is the plural of khuṭwah, from “to step”; the singular has an opening on its first letter, while the plural opens the first and dammas the second.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r2.anchor: فإذا أردت الواحدة قلت خطوة مفتوحة الأول

RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r3.claim: The phrase means the devil’s way and course: do not follow his traces or take his routes in listening to slander and spreading indecency among believers.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r3.anchor: لا تتبعوا آثار الشيطان ولا تسلكوا مسالكه

RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r4.claim: Although believers are specifically addressed, the ban applies to all accountable people, since everyone is forbidden to follow Satan’s steps.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r4.anchor: وإن خص بذلك المؤمنين فهو نهي لكل المكلفين

RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r5.claim: The conditional warning implies believers have not followed Satan; if the address meant unbelievers, they already had. God cautions believers after warning slanderers.

RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r6.claim: Faḥshāʾ is something whose ugliness is extreme.

RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r7.claim: Munkar is what people’s souls repudiate, recoil from, and do not approve.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161/r7.anchor: والمنكر ما تنكره النفوس فتنفر عنه ولا ترتضيه

RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r1.claim: Yaʿqūb and Ibn Muḥayṣin read mā zakkā with a doubled k.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ يعقوب وابن محيصن ما زكى بالتشديد

RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r2.claim: A zakī person has reached an approved level of obedience, like a crop that has matured; one is called purified only when actually pure.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r2.anchor: أن الزكي من بلغ في طاعة الله مبلغ الرضا

RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r3.claim: The author’s school argues tazkiya means producing purity in a subject, like blackening or reddening; the verse supports divine creation of purity.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r3.anchor: واحتج أصحابنا في مسألة المخلوق بقوله

RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r4.claim: The Muʿtazilites interpret tazkiya either as performing acts of grace (luṭf) or judging a servant pure.

RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r5.claim: Rāzī rejects the luṭf interpretation: if grace does not strengthen motive, it is irrelevant; if it does, its effect must be impossible, possible, or necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r5.anchor: أن فعل اللطف هل يرجح الداعي أو لا يرجحه

RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r6.claim: An impossible effect makes luṭf a deterrent; a merely possible effect occurs arbitrarily without a determinant; a necessary effect means God creates the servant’s act.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r6.anchor: فإن امتنع كان مانعا لا داعيا

RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r7.claim: The verse attaches purification to God’s will, whereas performing luṭf is obligatory and cannot depend on discretionary will.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r7.anchor: علق التزكية على المشيئة وفعل اللطف واجب

RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r8.claim: The verse calls purification grace and mercy, while creating acts of luṭf is obligatory, not discretionary favor.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r8.anchor: أنه علق التزكية على الفضل والرحمة

RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r9.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r9.claim: The second Muʿtazilite reading treats tazkiya as God’s judgment that the servant is pure.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r9.anchor: وأما الوجه الثاني : وهو الحكم بكونه زكيا

RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r10.claim: Rāzī rejects that reading: declaring someone pure is obligatory when true, since otherwise God would lie; it cannot depend on will.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r10.anchor: فذلك واجب لأنه لو يحكم به لكان كذبا

RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r11.claim: Rāzī concludes that the verse is explicit evidence for his school’s account of divine purification.
RAZI-FULL:v23p161#2/r11.anchor: فثبت أن قوله : { ولاكن الله يزكى من يشاء } نص في الباب

STUDYQURAN:24:10/r38.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r38.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r38.claim: Believers are told not to follow Satan's steps, which lead to indecency and wrongdoing.
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r38.anchor: Other verses that mention following in the footsteps of Satan include

STUDYQURAN:24:10/r39.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r39.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r39.claim: The Quran elsewhere says Satan commands evil or indecency, in 2:169 and 2:268.
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r39.anchor: That Satan commands to evil or indecency is also mentioned in

STUDYQURAN:24:10/r40.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r40.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r40.claim: Q glosses being purified as becoming upright or righteous, ṣāliḥ.
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r40.anchor: To be pure is understood here to mean to be upright or righteous (ṣāliḥ; Q)

STUDYQURAN:24:10/r41.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r41.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r41.claim: Another reported interpretation takes purity to mean being rightly guided.

STUDYQURAN:24:10/r42.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r42.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:24:10/r42.claim: Ṭ reports that purity here can mean following Islam.

TAB-FULL:v17p221/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p221/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p221/r1.claim: Without God's favor, mercy and compassion, people would have perished in the slander they indulged in and His punishment would have come swiftly.
TAB-FULL:v17p221/r1.anchor: لهلكتم فيما أفضتم فيه، وعاجلتكم من الله العقوبة.

TAB-FULL:v17p221/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p221/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p221/r2.claim: The conditional's answer is omitted because the listener can infer it from the following warning against following Satan's steps.
TAB-FULL:v17p221/r2.anchor: وترك ذكر الجواب لمعرفة السامع بالمراد من الكلام بعده، وهو قوله: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان} [النور: 21]

TAB-FULL:v17p221#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p221#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p221#2/r1.claim: Believers must not follow Satan's paths and traces by publicizing indecency among believers and repeating what its source has brought.
TAB-FULL:v17p221#2/r1.anchor: فإن الشيطان يأمر بالفحشاء وهي الزنا والمنكر من القول.

TAB-FULL:v17p221#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p221#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p221#2/r2.claim: Al-fāḥishah here means fornication, and al-munkar means evil speech.
TAB-FULL:v17p221#2/r2.anchor: فإن الشيطان يأمر بالفحشاء وهي الزنا والمنكر من القول.

TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r1.claim: Without God's favor and mercy, no one would be cleansed from the stain of sins and shirk; God purifies whoever He wills.
TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكا منكم من أحد أبدا} [النور: 21] قال: " ما زكى: ما أسلم "

TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that without God's favor no creature would find beneficial good or guard itself against harmful evil.
TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكا منكم من أحد أبدا} [النور: 21] يقول: «ما اهتدى منكم

TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets “was purified” as “became Muslim,” and generalizes that every Qur'anic occurrence of zakā or tazakkā means Islam.
TAB-FULL:v17p221#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكا منكم من أحد أبدا} [النور: 21] قال: " ما زكى: ما أسلم "

SULAMI:v2p42#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p42#4/r1.speaker: السياري
SULAMI:v2p42#4/r1.claim: The verse names God’s grace and mercy rather than worship, prayer, jihad, or good works to teach that even abundant worship is an effect of grace.
SULAMI:v2p42#4/r1.anchor: قال السياري : قال الله : ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ولم يقل

TABATABAI:11:108#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r1.claim: The verse's statement that no one would be purified without God's favor supports the allusion that good and happiness originate with God.
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r1.anchor: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم من أحد أبدا النور 21

TABATABAI:24:20-22/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī refers readers to his commentary on the parallel command in 2:208.
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r7.anchor: تقدم تفسير الآية في الآية 208 من سورة البقرة في الجزء الثاني من الكتاب

TABATABAI:24:20-22/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r8.claim: The repeated appeal to grace, now explicitly answered by ‘none would be purified,’ reflects that God alone bestows goodness and salvation; the Qur’an says good is in His hand and good that reaches people is from Him.
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r8.anchor: وهذا مما يدل عليه العقل فإن مفيض الخير والسعادة هو الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:24:20-22/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r9.claim: God wills to purify those prepared for purification who ask for it through their state of readiness; He hears their request and knows their preparedness.
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r9.anchor: ولا يشاء إلا تزكية من استعد لها وسأله بلسان استعداده ذلك

TABATABAI:24:20-22/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r10.claim: God is hearing of the request for purification and knowing of the person’s readiness for it.
TABATABAI:24:20-22/r10.anchor: أي سميع لسؤال من سأله التزكية عليم بحال من استعد لها

THALABI:v7p80#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p80#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p80#2/r1.claim: Satan commands indecency and wrongdoing; without God’s grace and mercy no one could ever be purified, but God purifies whom He wills from sin through mercy and forgiveness.
THALABI:v7p80#2/r1.anchor: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم من أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء والله سميع عليم

THALABI:v7p80#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p80#2/r2.speaker: ابن محيص ويعقوب
THALABI:v7p80#2/r2.claim: Ibn Muhaysin and Yaqub read zakkā with a doubled k, meaning purified; the later verb yuzakkī supports this reading.
THALABI:v7p80#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيص ويعقوب: زكى بالتشديد أي طهر، دليلها قوله سبحانه وتعالى ولكن الله يزكي

THALABI:v7p80#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p80#2/r4.speaker: أبو الدرداء
THALABI:v7p80#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet warning that uninformed support in a dispute incurs divine anger, blocking enforcement of a divine limit defies God, and falsely spreading a damaging accusation against a Muslim merits the Fire; he links this to the Qur’anic condemnation of spreading indecency.
THALABI:v7p80#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أيما رجل شد عضد امرئ من الناس في خصومة لا علم له بها فهو في ظل سخط الله

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p302/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p302/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p302/r1.anchor: ما زكا منكم من أحد} أي ما طهر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r1.claim: Muqātil identifies Satan's steps with his beautification of the slander against ʿĀʾisha.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني تزيين الشيطان في قذف عائشة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes them as disobedience to God and everything God dislikes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بعصيان الله وكل ما يكره الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r3.speaker: مقاتل، الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r3.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī explain them as sins and acts unrecognized by religious law or prophetic practice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل (¬5)، والكلبي: بالمعاصي وما لا يعرف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r4.speaker: مقاتل، أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r4.claim: Muqātil and Abū Zayd gloss زكى as becoming sound or righteous.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r4.anchor: ما صلح. قاله مقاتل، وأبو زيد (¬7). والزكاة تكون (¬8) بمعنى الصلاح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses زكى as becoming purified.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r6.claim: Some apply the statement generally: without God's favor no one would be guided or made righteous.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r6.anchor: وأجرى بعضهم هذه الآية على العموم وقال: معناها أن الله تعالى يخبر أنه لولا فضله ورحمته (¬2) ما اهتدى أحد ولا صلح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r7.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r7.claim: Others restrict the address to those who took part in the slander against ʿĀʾisha.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r7.anchor: والآخرون يقولون: المراد بهذا الخطاب الذين خاضوا في حديث الإفك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r8.claim: In a report via ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn ʿAbbās says no one involved would have received acceptance of repentance; the author explains purification and repair after the sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p170/r8.anchor: وهو معنى قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء، قال- في قوله: {ما زكى منكم من أحد أبدا} -: ما قبل توبة أحد منكم أبدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains God's purification as His having willed to accept their repentance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: فقد شئت أن أتوب عليكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses God's purification as making someone righteous.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r3.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r3.claim: Another explanation is that God purifies whom He wills from sin by mercy and forgiveness, guiding that person to repent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r3.anchor: وقال غيره (¬9): يطهر من يشاء من

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r4.claim: God hears their words and knows the remorse and repentance within them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p171/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {سميع} لقولكم {عليم} بما في نفوسكم من الندامة والتوبة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:19-22/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:19-22/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:19-22/r3.claim: None of those who became involved in the slander would have been purified of that sin without God's favor and mercy; He purifies whom He wills through forgiveness.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:19-22/r3.anchor: ما صلح وطهر من هذا الذنب أحد { منكم } يعني: من الذين خاضوا فيه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r1.claim: The steps of Satan mean sins.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r1.anchor: قوله: {يأيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات} [النور: 21] خطايا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r2.claim: Some say the steps are Satan's commands.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r3.claim: The pronoun in this clause refers to Satan.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r4.claim: Satan commands people to sin and to commit shameful and wrongful deeds.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r5.speaker: أبو مجلز
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p434#2/r5.claim: Abu Majliz says the steps of Satan include vows to commit sins.
